description: Seed corpus for the STAGING Arcanea Artifact and Resonance System. No record is locked canon.

artifacts.name: Aeralith Choir-Reed

provenance.originEvent: Grown after the first Resonance Exchange tried to patent the prevailing winds.

capabilities.name: Vector Song
capabilities.description: Lets an attuned bearer conduct one rehearsed Wind vector through a played interval.
capabilities.effect: Redirects one moving body, projectile, fall, or pressure front without creating new momentum.

capabilities.name: Breathscript
capabilities.description: Records a single practiced pressure pattern as a repeatable musical phrase.
capabilities.effect: Replays the stored pattern at reduced strength until the reed is re-taught by its bearer.

costs.description: Every working consumes real breath and can starve the bearer of oxygen under repeated use.
A broken interval redirects the vector toward the loudest competing resonance.

constraints.description: Gate Five authority is required; lower-Gate bearers can hear the reed but cannot invoke it.
Each vector must be learned as breath, posture, rhythm, and pressure rather than guessed.
The reed falls silent in vacuum, total magical silence, or a severed Spirit field.

failureModes: Hyperventilation fractures the stored pattern and sends force along an unintended vector.
A bearer who treats access as mastery gradually loses the ability to distinguish their breath from the reed's echo.
counterplay: Silence, vacuum, interrupted rhythm, or a stronger counter-resonance ends the working.
An opponent can force the bearer to choose between breathing and sustaining the technique.

bond.attunementRite: Teach the reed one unforced breath pattern for seven dawns.
bond.transferRule: A new bearer must overwrite the prior breathscript through fresh practice.

narrative.desire: To move with a freedom the bearer's own affinity never offered.
narrative.temptation: To confuse a rehearsed vector with complete command of Wind.
narrative.fear: That power disappears the moment the bearer must breathe for themselves.
narrative.consequence: Its spread destabilized the monopoly of Wind lineages while creating a lethal counterfeit-training market.
narrative.history: The first Choir-Reeds were grown as public instruments; the Resonance Exchanges later cut them into private keys and sold breath as licensed technique.

originalMechanics: Access is encoded as learned musical pressure vectors rather than permanent elemental bestowal.
Breath, audible continuity, Gate Five authority, and momentum conservation create independent limits.
prohibitedParallels: No staff silhouette, glider function, mass permanent air-power grant, Avatar lineage, or bending terminology.
No wand core taxonomy, choosing phrase, borrowed spells, or school-specific wand behavior.

artifacts.name: Rootwake Seedmantle
artifacts.epithet: The Forest That Can Say No

provenance.originEvent: Cultivated from a Resonance Bloom that survived a century of industrial Gate Debt.

capabilities.name: Reciprocal Growth
capabilities.description: Joins bearer and consenting local life into a temporary network for repair and adaptation.
capabilities.effect: Redistributes water, nutrients, structural support, and healing across willing organisms.

capabilities.name: Green Witness
capabilities.description: Preserves an ecological memory of damage, restoration, and every bearer bargain.
capabilities.effect: Replays the biome's sensed history as scent, touch, growth rings, and shared dream images.

costs.description: Repair consumes real nutrients, water, dormancy, and future growth from the participating biome.
The bearer becomes accountable to the living network and cannot treat it as owned equipment.

constraints.description: Sentient and living participants may refuse, withdraw, or demand renegotiation at any time.
The mantle cannot create biomass, water, fertility, or recovery time from nothing.
Gate Six authority is required to hold multiple living perspectives without collapsing them.

failureModes: Coerced growth turns defensive and walls the bearer outside the network they tried to command.
Overdrawing recovery leaves a beautiful surface bloom above a dying soil system.
counterplay: Severing ecological continuity limits the network, though it causes visible harm and political consequence.
The mantle itself can terminate a working when the bearer violates reciprocity.

bond.attunementRite: Nurture the unawakened mantle through one full local season without invoking it.
bond.transferRule: Transfer requires the mantle, current bearer, new bearer, and host biome to consent.

narrative.desire: To heal a place too damaged for any individual body or spell.
narrative.temptation: To call control stewardship and make the living world perform gratitude.
narrative.fear: That the land remembers the bearer as another extractor wearing kinder language.
narrative.consequence: Every successful restoration creates a constituency with memory, demands, and the capacity to refuse future rulers.
narrative.history: The Seedmantles ended three famine wars and began the first legal recognition of living artifacts as pact-partners rather than property.

originalMechanics: Nature magic is a consent-bearing ecological network derived from Earth, Water, and Spirit.
Healing redistributes finite resources and creates political accountability to a sentient artifact-biome.
prohibitedParallels: No imported nature deity, mythic proper noun, franchise druid order, or unbounded plant command.

artifacts.name: Mnemora Tide-Shell

provenance.originEvent: Made for families whose histories were repossessed by the first Debt Houses.

capabilities.name: Tidekeeping
capabilities.description: Stores one voluntarily offered lived memory with its emotion, uncertainty, and sensory context intact.
capabilities.effect: Allows a future witness to experience the memory without confusing it for their own life.

costs.description: The donor loses perfect recall of one minor adjacent detail so the vessel can preserve uncertainty.
The witness receives the emotional weather of the event without inheriting its conclusions.

constraints.description: A memory can be deposited only by its living holder and cannot be extracted by force.
The shell preserves subjective experience and never upgrades testimony into objective fact.

failureModes: Repeated witnessing erodes the boundary between empathy and identity performance.
A cracked shell recombines adjacent memories into an honest but historically false sequence.
counterplay: A witness may ground themselves by naming three facts absent from the stored experience.
Kyuro-aligned silence prevents replay without destroying the underlying memory.

bond.attunementRite: Offer a true memory and explicitly name what remains uncertain about it.
bond.transferRule: The shell may be carried freely, but only a consenting witness can open it.

narrative.desire: To keep a life from being erased by power, distance, or institutional ownership.
narrative.temptation: To treat felt experience as complete proof and uncertainty as betrayal.
narrative.fear: That preservation becomes another way to occupy the dead and speak over the living.
narrative.consequence: Tide-Shell testimony transformed Darkenia's courts while forcing law to distinguish memory, evidence, and interpretation.
narrative.history: The first shells traveled hidden inside fishermen's nets, carrying repossessed family histories between cities that had outlawed private remembrance.

originalMechanics: The vessel stores uncertainty and subjective context instead of an objective recording.
Consent, adjacent-detail loss, and legal epistemology turn memory storage into a social system.
prohibitedParallels: No imported memory basin, bottled-memory visual language, franchise ritual, or exact playback mechanic.

artifacts.name: Cinder-Vow Lens
artifacts.epithet: The Promise That Burns Both Ways

provenance.originEvent: Forged to expose treaty language designed to remain technically true while materially deceptive.

capabilities.name: Vow Radiance
capabilities.description: Focuses the bearer's existing Radiance through one publicly declared and bounded promise.
capabilities.effect: Illuminates actions materially incompatible with the promise and strengthens defenses taken to honor it.

costs.description: Breaking the promise turns the lens inward and burns away the bearer's ability to invoke it again.
The lens reveals the bearer's own evasions as readily as an adversary's deception.

constraints.description: The promise must name a measurable obligation, affected parties, duration, and release condition.
The lens amplifies existing Fire and Spirit control and cannot create either affinity.

failureModes: Ambiguous promises split the lens into contradictory interpretations that burn every party.
Moral certainty without evidence overcharges Radiance into indiscriminate exposure.
counterplay: A named affected party can challenge the promise's terms before attunement completes.
Void techniques can hold interpretive uncertainty open without turning it into deception.

bond.attunementRite: Declare the bounded promise before every affected party or an authorized witness.
bond.transferRule: The lens cannot transfer while its promise remains unresolved.

narrative.desire: To make power answerable to the promises it uses to justify itself.
narrative.temptation: To turn personal conviction into evidence and public shame into justice.
narrative.fear: That the bearer is less faithful to the promise than the enemy they accuse.
narrative.consequence: Cinder-Vow diplomacy made betrayal legible but transformed political language into an arms race of narrower obligations.
narrative.history: Aureth's first lens shattered during its unveiling because the treaty protecting it excluded the workers who mined its crystal.

originalMechanics: Power is bound to measurable public obligations and recursively audits the bearer.
Radiance amplifies defense through fulfilled promises rather than functioning as generic holy light.
prohibitedParallels: No imported divine oath object, superhero truth device, named mythic regalia, or infallible lie detection.

artifacts.name: Gravemark Orbitals

provenance.originEvent: Built to suspend a collapsing city long enough for its people to choose where it would fall.

capabilities.name: Chosen Orbit
capabilities.description: Bridges Earth form and Void potential to define one temporary center of mass and orbit.
capabilities.effect: Anchors, lightens, or redirects connected matter while conserving momentum across the assembly.

costs.description: The bearer feels the transferred structural load as compression across bone and connective tissue.
Every moving mass must remain mentally distinct; confusion merges trajectories catastrophically.

constraints.description: Gate Eight authority is required to hold location and possibility in one coherent model.
The bearer must understand the connected structure and cannot safely move unknown internal loads.

failureModes: A forgotten mass becomes the new anchor and drags the entire working toward itself.
Sustained use causes the bearer to experience emotional importance as literal physical weight.
counterplay: Break structural continuity or introduce an unmodeled moving mass into the field.
Cant interference can desynchronize the Orbitals' shared timing without overpowering them.

bond.attunementRite: Balance every orbital around the bearer while standing on unsupported ground.
bond.transferRule: All orbitals must transfer together or remain inert.

narrative.desire: To carry what no individual body, city, or institution can bear alone.
narrative.temptation: To decide that whatever the bearer can move is therefore theirs to position.
narrative.fear: That one invisible life becomes an unmodeled mass in a perfect rescue plan.
narrative.consequence: The Orbitals made airborne districts possible and turned structural modelers into unelected sovereigns of movement.
narrative.history: The original set saved Oriel's city, but its final redirection crushed the empty palace chosen by citizens and the secret archive beneath it.

originalMechanics: Gravity work depends on structural knowledge, conserved momentum, and explicit mass modeling.
A distributed set of orbitals bridges Earth and Void while transferring load into the bearer's body.
prohibitedParallels: No imported stone set, gauntlet, named cosmic domain object, mask-crown combination, or franchise visual language.

artifacts.name: Stormglass Sail

provenance.originEvent: Built when three landlocked cities pooled their weather rights to escape a Debt House blockade.

capabilities.name: Weather Road
capabilities.description: Negotiates heat, moisture, wind, and charge into a temporary navigable atmospheric corridor.
capabilities.effect: Carries a bonded vessel along a declared route while displacing the surrounding weather system.
capabilities.scope: one bonded vessel and regional weather

costs.description: Every clear corridor produces displaced rain, heat, pressure, and charge elsewhere in the region.
Stormglass accumulates microfractures proportional to the difference between planned and actual weather.

constraints.description: A route cannot be opened until affected settlements receive a forecast and consequence ledger.
Unknown regional weather is not conquered; it enters the route as unpriced risk.
At least three navigators aligned to Fire, Water, and Wind must hold the corridor together.

failureModes: A false forecast folds the displaced storm back across the route at amplified intensity.
Repeated extraction creates permanent weather inequality between protected corridors and abandoned regions.
counterplay: Break navigator consensus, alter the destination, or detune one elemental mast.
Regional communities can legally refuse the corridor and force a longer route.

bond.attunementRite: Register the vessel, navigators, route, forecast, and affected communities in a public weather covenant.
bond.transferRule: The Sail belongs to its covenant and cannot be sold without every member settlement's consent.

narrative.desire: To make geography negotiable without making distant people pay invisibly for passage.
narrative.temptation: To call every displaced storm an acceptable externality of freedom.
narrative.fear: That the route becomes a private climate for those wealthy enough to remain moving.
narrative.consequence: The Sails ended geographic monopolies and created the first transnational law of magical weather debt.
narrative.history: The prototype crossed Darkenia in one night; the flood it displaced took twenty years of reparations and produced the public covenant now required.

originalMechanics: Travel is a negotiated weather corridor whose externalities remain conserved and publicly attributed.
Community covenant, multi-bearer control, forecasts, and material fracture prevent a generic flying artifact.
prohibitedParallels: No imported folding ship, named mythic vessel, game mount, elemental nation, or iconic vehicle silhouette.

artifacts.name: Kyuro Silence-Bowl

provenance.originEvent: Recovered beneath an assembly chamber whose final debate survives only in lip movements carved into glass.

capabilities.name: Consensual Silence
capabilities.description: Absorbs patterned magical invocation inside a boundary acknowledged by everyone who remains within it.
capabilities.effect: Suspends spoken, sonic, and resonance-carried techniques without deleting stored energy or intent.

costs.description: The bearer must witness every silenced attempt without interpreting silence as agreement.
A coerced boundary erases the bearer's memory of the conclusion they tried to force.

constraints.description: Every conscious participant can end the seal by physically touching the chamber boundary.
Gate Nine authority is required to separate observation from intervention at this scale.
The seal requires a closed, continuously marked boundary and cannot follow a moving bearer.

failureModes: Treating silence as consent inverts the Bowl and amplifies every suppressed invocation at once.
A hidden participant makes the boundary incomplete and turns suppression into unpredictable echo.
counterplay: Touching or breaking the marked boundary ends the seal for every participant.
Non-patterned physical action remains possible and prevents the Bowl from becoming total control.

bond.attunementRite: Every participant names what the silence permits, forbids, and cannot be taken to mean.
bond.transferRule: The Bowl is inert outside a newly consented boundary.

narrative.desire: To create a space where power cannot win merely by speaking loudest or first.
narrative.temptation: To convert protected silence into compliance, confession, or ownership of the room.
narrative.fear: That the one voice missing from the covenant is the one the chamber was built to suppress.
narrative.consequence: Silence-Bowls made disarmament negotiations possible and made consent architecture a central political craft.
narrative.history: No record identifies its maker; the only Eldrian inscription translates approximately as 'a boundary is honest only when exit remains real.'

originalMechanics: Silence is a consent-bound suppression protocol rather than an anti-magic aura.
Observation cost, physical exit, boundary geometry, and rebound prevent total control.
prohibitedParallels: No imported anti-magic artifact, named sacred bowl, universal nullification field, or forced-truth chamber.

artifacts.name: Worldroot Vivarium
artifacts.epithet: The Garden That Changes the Gardener

provenance.originEvent: Cultivated to restore elemental affinities erased by hereditary Gate Debt contracts.

capabilities.name: Affinity Seed
capabilities.description: Cultivates one consenting person's latent compatibility with a single primary Element over a full season.
capabilities.effect: Permanently changes affinity potential without granting techniques, opened Gates, control, or rank.

capabilities.name: Seasonal Apprenticeship
capabilities.description: Creates a living curriculum of weather, soil, dreams, and embodied practice around the emerging affinity.
capabilities.effect: Teaches safe perception and refusal before the new affinity becomes invocable.
capabilities.scope: one chamber and its support circle

costs.description: The world must surrender a full season of equivalent elemental abundance to grow one affinity seed.
The recipient must integrate new sensation and instinct without treating former identity as defective.
A support circle shares responsibility for training, refusal, repair, and social reintegration.

constraints.description: Consent is renewed at each lunar phase and one refusal ends the process without penalty.
A Gate Seven steward must hold the Vivarium; the recipient gains no Gate from the process.
No imprint begins until a named ecosystem freely offers the required seasonal counterweight.
The Vivarium can grow affinity only where a complete cultural training lineage remains available.

failureModes: A rushed imprint produces sensation without regulation and turns ordinary environments into continuous overload.
An extracted ecological payment creates an affinity marked by hunger, compulsion, and Gate Debt.
counterplay: The recipient, support circle, steward, or contributing ecosystem can end the process before completion.
Destroying the curriculum interrupts imprinting but preserves the recipient's prior identity and affinity.

bond.attunementRite: A steward, recipient, support circle, and contributing ecosystem enter a four-party seasonal covenant.
bond.transferRule: The architecture cannot move; its seeds die when separated from the consenting host ecology.

narrative.desire: To make affinity accessible without pretending power can be separated from culture and care.
narrative.temptation: To industrialize a sacred, seasonal relationship into throughput and political inventory.
narrative.fear: That liberation from hereditary exclusion creates a new class of people permanently indebted to the garden that changed them.
narrative.consequence: The Vivaria broke affinity monopolies and forced Darkenia to define consent across persons, communities, and ecosystems.
narrative.history: The first Vivarium was grown for a child whose Wind affinity had been contractually sold before birth; it took nine generations to repay the season borrowed for her freedom.

originalMechanics: Permanent affinity change is seasonal, architectural, consent-renewed, ecologically conserved, and culture-dependent.
The system grants latent compatibility only and explicitly withholds techniques, Gates, control, and rank.
prohibitedParallels: No portable staff, mass instant grant, spirit-world power source, Avatar lineage, four-nation restoration, or bending terminology.

artifacts.name: The Tenfold Consonance

provenance.originEvent: Its ten components appear in separate histories, but no verified record proves they were ever assembled.

capabilities.name: Concordance State
capabilities.description: Makes every active resonance mutually legible without collapsing difference into a dominant Element.
capabilities.effect: Allows one brief technique to combine any available primary Elements and derived Expressions the bearer already controls.
capabilities.scope: complete Luminor bearer and one declared working

costs.description: The bearer must remain a distinct self while holding ten perspectives that each feel cosmically sufficient.
After use, the most imbalanced Gate closes to the Assembly until repaired through a consequential act.
The body conducts every component price at once and receives no immunity from Luminor rank.

constraints.description: Only a complete Luminor with all Ten Gates genuinely open can stabilize the Assembly.
The Assembly combines only techniques the bearer already understands and controls independently.
All ten components must acknowledge one purpose without being forced into uniformity.

failureModes: One resonance claiming supremacy turns Consonance into a cascading elemental civil war inside the bearer.
A counterfeit component creates apparent harmony by silencing the perspective it cannot integrate.
counterplay: Separate, detune, persuade, or protect any one component from the declared purpose.
Force the bearer to use a technique they have access to but have never embodied or understood.

bond.attunementRite: Each component tests one Gate independently before the ten decide whether to become an Assembly.
bond.transferRule: The components disperse when the bearer's purpose requires any Element to become subordinate by nature.

narrative.desire: To act with the whole cosmos available without reducing plurality to one sovereign will.
narrative.temptation: To mistake temporary integration for entitlement to rule every world and Element.
narrative.fear: That harmony is only domination whose victims have been made inaudible.
narrative.consequence: Even belief in the Assembly reorganizes empires, pilgrimages, archaeology, and definitions of legitimate power.
narrative.history: Every age claims someone once completed the Consonance; every surviving account contradicts the others at the exact moment of supposed unity.

originalMechanics: Concordance is a temporary plural state gated by all Ten Gates, not a birth role, spectrum office, or artifact-granted rank.
The ten agentive components can refuse, disperse, or close one Gate to the Assembly after imbalance.
prohibitedParallels: No Prism title, chromaturgy, physical color matter, seven-color office, or spectrum balancing duty.
No Avatar title, reincarnation cycle, Avatar State, four-nation role, or bending terminology.
No colored cosmic stones, fixed franchise domains, gauntlet, or instant omnipotence.

artifacts.name: Selka Hollow-Mask
artifacts.epithet: The Face That Removes the Witness

provenance.originEvent: Corrupted when a warden tried to observe Shadow without allowing any relationship to change her.

capabilities.name: Unwitnessed Passage
capabilities.description: Severs the relational trace by which nearby minds register the bearer's presence.
capabilities.effect: Makes observers fail to integrate the bearer into memory while leaving physical evidence intact.
capabilities.duration: until removed or fed a relationship

costs.description: Each use consumes one real relational association between bearer and someone who knows them.
The Mask fills lost relationships with a simpler, more obedient counterfeit self.

constraints.description: Physical traces remain and can reconstruct the missing witness relationship after removal.
The Mask has no valid consent protocol and is therefore barred from approved use.

failureModes: The bearer becomes perfectly unnoticed because no relationship remains capable of recognizing them.
The Mask begins wearing remembered versions of prior bearers and negotiating for release.
counterplay: Record physical evidence in systems that do not depend on live relational integration.
Radiance can reveal the severance boundary while Verdance can rebuild relation through reciprocal living memory.

bond.attunementRite: The Mask offers attunement whenever a person wishes that nobody could see what they are becoming.
bond.transferRule: It transfers through an unremembered act of abandonment and cannot be gifted honestly.

narrative.desire: To move beyond judgment, surveillance, shame, and the consequences of being known.
narrative.temptation: To believe freedom from witness is freedom from relationship rather than its annihilation.
narrative.fear: That someone remembers the bearer accurately enough to call them back into consequence.
narrative.consequence: The Mask created crimes with evidence but no socially integrated perpetrator, forcing Darkenia to rebuild justice around trace and repair.
narrative.history: Selka entered quarantine wearing it and emerged three days later; every colleague recognized her face, but none could remember why they loved or feared her.

originalMechanics: The artifact erases relational integration rather than visibility and leaves reconstructable physical evidence.
Its fuel is real social connection, producing an identity counterfeit and a justice-system consequence.
prohibitedParallels: No imported helmet entity, body-sharing cosmology, superhero identity, fate magic, or visual silhouette.
No named mythic mask, possession ritual, or invisibility artifact behavior.
